test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If the current flowing through a resistance of 5 ohm is 6 amp, then the current flowing through another resistance of 10 ohm connected in series to it is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 amp**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When two resistors are connected in series, the **current remains the same** throughout the circuit as it has only one path to flow.
 
• The total resistance in the circuit is calculated as the **sum of individual resistances**. For the given problem, **total resistance = 5 Ω + 10 Ω = 15 Ω**.
 
• By Ohm's Law (V = IR), the voltage across the circuit can be calculated using the current and total resistance. Here, **voltage = 6 amp × 15 Ω = 90 volts**.
 
• The current flowing through each resistor in series remains constant, i.e., **6 amp**, regardless of the individual resistance values.
 
• Hence, the **current flowing through the 10 Ω resistor** is **6 amp**, same as the current through the 5 Ω resistor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• It states that the current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points.
 
• Mathematically, V = IR, where R is the resistance.
 
• It is the foundational principle for analyzing electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit:**
 
 
• A circuit where components are connected end-to-end, forming a single path for current flow.
 
• In a series circuit, the current remains the same through all components, but the voltage divides proportionally across each component.
 
 
 
• **Resistance:**
 
 
• It is a measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current in a material.
 
• Measured in Ohms (Ω), resistance depends on the material, length, and cross-sectional area of the conductor.
 
 
 
• **Important Formula for Series Circuits:**
 
 
• Total Resistance **(Rₜₒₜₐₗ) = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ**.
 
• Total Voltage **(Vₜₒₜₐₗ) = V₁ + V₂ + ... + Vₙ**.
 
• Current (I) remains constant throughout the circuit.
